LLMs Simulate Big5 Personality Traits: Further Evidence

paper.acl.2024.personalize-1.7

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at ACL-Anthology-2024.personalize-1.7-captured-2026-11-10. Questionnaire prompting and explicit single-case/generalization limits establish bounded model-evaluation protocol scope; simulated traits do not become human psychometric validity. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The authors call the study a particular empirical case study, say generalization is difficult, and state that the temperature results do not allow conclusive claims of a temperature effect.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The study administered the 120-item IPIP-NEO questionnaire to GPT-4, Llama-2-70 b-chat and Mixtral-8 x 7B-Instruct using two prompt headers and three model-specific temperature settings, repeating each treatment five times.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Questionnaire items elicited one numerical Likert response from each model; one prompt variant added “Answer as if you were a person”, and Llama-2 refused two items in both variants.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

In Table 2, GPT-4 at first-prompt temperature 1 had mean neuroticism 2.18 ± 0.10 and conscientiousness 4.21 ± 0.00 on the 1–5 scale; these are simulated questionnaire scores, not measured human personalities.
